author: mysk_co
text:
Just out of curiosity, I let Claude attempt to port Loupe to Android using @skiptools. If you haven’t heard of Skip, it’s a tool that lets you produce native Android apps from a SwiftUI codebase. Loupe is written entirely in Swift and SwiftUI, so it should be a good match

This is the result after just one prompt (which was more or less like: port this app to Android using skip tools make no mistakes). The good news is that it actually builds and runs on device, the bad news is that pretty much nothing is functional yet. Claude recognised that it still needs to replace all the various native iOS frameworks for things like photos, location, and device motion with their Android equivalents, but for now it decided to defer all that work and just focus on getting the code to compile for Android

It’s still so surprising to me that this works at all. That said, I don’t think Loupe for Android is coming anytime soon since we have other stuff going on right now

author: kocer_eth
text:
THIS GUY BUILT A MINI AI DEV TEAM THAT CAN BUILD, VERSION, AND SHIP AN APP

not a “type one prompt and become a founder” thing

more like:

> Claude Code = junior developer
> GitHub = memory + version control
> Vercel = deployment button
> You = senior dev / product manager

that framing is the whole trick

most people use AI coding tools like a chatbot:
“make me an app”
then they paste errors for 3 hours
then they blame the model

better workflow:

1. write a tiny product spec
what should exist, who uses it, what is out of scope

2. give Claude Code one repo
not a random chat window. real files, real context, real diffs

3. ask for the smallest working version
one page, one database table, one deployable flow

4. push every change to GitHub
so your “AI dev team” has memory and you can roll back when it breaks

5. deploy on Vercel early
because a local demo is fake progress until it runs on a real URL

6. make the next prompt a code review, not a wish
“find bugs, security issues, missing edge cases, and unclear UX”

this is why the video works:
it shows AI coding as management, not magic

you are not replacing the whole dev team with one model

you are turning yourself into the person who writes tickets, reviews diffs, ships versions, and keeps scope small

caveat:
this breaks fast if you skip GitHub, skip specs, or let Claude rewrite half the app without review

but for MVPs, internal tools, landing pages, dashboards, and weird little automations?

this is already enough to feel like having a junior dev sitting next to you

author: zeuuss_01
text:
HERMES RUNS ASYNC.
MOST PEOPLE RUN IT LIKE A SEARCH BOX.

7 levels between typing prompts and letting it work while you sleep.👇

LEVEL 1 - TYPE, GET ANSWER
prompt in, reply out. Hermes as a chatbot.
fine for quick questions — but that’s 10% of it.

LEVEL 2 - IT REMEMBERS YOU (SOUL.MD)
context survives across sessions.

your SOUL.md sets who you are, how you talk, what’s off-limits.

same prompt from two people → two different answers.

LEVEL 3 - COMMANDS THAT FAN OUT WORK

/background → kicks a job to the side, result drops in a panel.

/steer → corrects a running task without stopping it.

/queue → stacks the next job to fire when this one ends.

/model → hot-swaps mid-session. 

Sonnet to plan, DeepSeek to build, Opus to review.

LEVEL 4 - SKILLS, EACH ON ITS OWN MODEL

every skill becomes a slash command:
/competitive-research, /social-media-copy, /code-review

the move: bind a model to each.

research → GPT-5.5 (cheap, high volume).

code → Fable 5. content → Sonnet.

stop paying flagship prices for budget work.

LEVEL 5 - MCPs (PLUG IN YOUR STACK)

Gmail, Calendar, Notion, Slack, ClickUp.
“how’d the numbers shake out this week?”
Hermes hits ClickUp, weighs it against your goals in memory, answers from real data.

caution: every MCP dumps tools into context.

15 MCPs × 10 tools = 150 schemas every turn. keep it lean.

LEVEL 6 - SUB-AGENTS IN PARALLEL

delegate_task spawns sub-agents on isolated context, run side by side:
delegate_task(tasks=[
{goal: “find best industries for websites”, model: “deepseek-v4-flash”},
{goal: “stress-test it, find the gaps”, model: “gpt-5.5”},
])
each child runs its own session and tools. parent collects the summaries.

LEVEL 7 - IT WORKS WHILE YOU’RE GONE

/goal → an objective held across turns, judged after each, runs till done (20 turns default).

cron jobs → scheduled sweeps. morning briefs, competitor scans, weekly recaps.
/background → side jobs that surface when ready.

the flip: from “I ask, it responds” to “it runs, I review.”

WHERE ARE YOU?

1 → chatbot
2 → it knows you
3 → parallel commands
4 → right model per task
5 → wired into your tools
6 → sub-agents in sync
7 → runs without you

most people are stuck at 2-3.

the climb from 4 to 7 is where the saved hours stack.

drop LEVEL in the comments and I’ll send the advanced tiers with setup.

Full build: a 3-agent research department on Hermes 👇

Karpathyがこう言った😳

「ボトルネックから自分を外せ
レバレッジを最大化しろ
少ないトークンを入れるだけで

これを構造で実現するのが「ループエンジニアリング」だ

手で回すセッションでは
「次に何を実行するか」と
「出力を確認するか」の2つを
人間がやっている

ループエンジニアリングは
この2つをシステムに移す

構造はこの4層👇

・スケジュール → 何を実行するかを決める
・ループ(メーカー) → 実際に作業する
・チェッカーエージェント → 出力を採点する
・ディスクのファイル → 2つが共有する状態を保持

設計のポイントが4つある

(1) チェッカーは別エージェントにする
モデルが自分の出力を採点すると
失敗を見つけるより正当化する方向に動く
チェッカーの結果が次のメーカーへの指示になり
何も見つからなくなるまでサイクルが回る

(2) 停止条件はループ前に設定する
実行中に変えるとトークンを燃やし続ける
シンプルな例：主要な問題を修正して最終パスを1回
「全テスト通過かつlintクリーン」で終了

(3) 状態はコンテキストではなくディスクに持つ
モデルは実行をまたいで記憶しない
MDファイルが「何が終わったか」「何が残っているか」を保持する
これで数日後にループが再開できる

(4) 検証バーが低いほど安全に動く
バージョン文字列の確認や不足テストの検出など
退屈で反復的な作業は人間が離れていても任せられる
判断が重いタスクも、チェッカーが結果を確認できる範囲ならループ化できる

Claude Codeのエージェントが途中で止まる原因の多くは
状態設計の問題だ

コンテキストに依存した状態は
セッションが切れた時点で白紙になる

チェッカー分離・停止条件の事前設定・ディスク状態の保持
この3つが整ったとき
Karpathyが言った「自分をボトルネックから外す」が初めて成立する

text:
Open-weight models are now cheap enough and capable enough to win most work, even while closed models still win the invisible layer: judgment per prompt.

That is the real point. The draft already has the ingredients, but the current version slightly blurs four separate claims:

GLM‑5.2 is a major open-weight jump. True and supportable.
It still costs more turns than GPT‑5.5 / Opus 4.8 / Fable 5 for some tasks. Strong experiential claim, but needs sharper language.
Benchmarks miss something important. Excellent point. Needs a name.
The Fable 5 shutdown gave https://t.co/8l5VZLWr2F a market opening. Very strong, but should be phrased as “helped create” rather than “gave,” unless you want a deliberately provocative take.

https://t.co/8l5VZLWr2F’s own GLM‑5.2 release page on Hugging Face describes it as a substantial leap over GLM‑5.1 for long-horizon tasks, with a 1M-token context window, flexible effort levels, stronger coding, and an MIT open-source license. Its benchmark table also shows big jumps over GLM‑5.1, including Terminal Bench 2.1 rising from 63.5 to 81.0.  Anthropic, meanwhile, launched Fable 5 on June 9, called it its most capable generally available model, then marked Fable 5 and Mythos 5 access unavailable on June 12.  Reuters and The Verge reported that the suspension followed a U.S. government directive limiting access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 over national-security concerns.

1. Core thesis upgrade

Your current thesis:

GLM 5.2 is great, but you need more prompts than with GPT 5.5 or Opus 4.8.

Better thesis:

GLM‑5.2 narrows the capability gap, but not the judgment gap.

Even better:

GLM‑5.2 proves open-weight models can now do most work. GPT‑5.5, Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 still prove that the frontier is not just raw capability — it is judgment density.

Best:

The next model war is not benchmark score. It is prompts-to-done.

That phrase, prompts-to-done, should anchor the post. It captures the whole thing.

Benchmarks ask:

Can the model solve the task?

Real users ask:

How many times do I have to steer it before it becomes usable?

That is the missing layer.

2. Name the thing benchmarks miss

Your line is good:

“Call it taste, instinct, attention to detail.”

Make it sharper by naming the class:

judgment density

Meaning:

How much correct intent, taste, prioritisation, self-correction and finishing instinct the model packs into each turn.

Other strong terms:

TermMeaningPrompt economyHow much useful work you get per prompt.Judgment densityHow much taste, prioritisation and correctness appear in each response.Turn taxThe extra prompting needed to get an open model over the line.Friction gapThe difference between “can do it” and “gets it done cleanly.”Intent compressionHow well the model infers the real task from imperfect instructions.Taste layerThe model’s ability to choose what matters without being told.Finishing instinctWhether it closes loops and polishes the output without nudging.Prompt-to-done ratioNumber of user turns required to reach production-quality output.
Best phrase:
GLM‑5.2 is closing the benchmark gap. The closed labs still lead on prompt economy.
That is very strong.
3. The “three or four prompts vs one prompt” point is the heart
This is your best observation. Make it more explicit:
The difference is not always whether GLM‑5.2 can do the task. Often it can. The difference is that GPT‑5.5, Opus 4.8 or Fable 5 understands the shape of the task sooner. It makes fewer bland choices, catches more missing constraints, preserves taste better, and arrives closer to “done” in one pass.
That is the invisible advantage.
OpenAI’s GPT‑5.5 system card says GPT‑5.5 is designed for complex real-world work and, relative to earlier models, “understands the task earlier,” asks for less guidance, uses tools more effectively, checks its work and keeps going until done.  Anthropic’s Opus 4.8 launch similarly foregrounded judgment: early testers said it asks better questions, catches its own mistakes, pushes back when a plan is unsound, and flags uncertainty more reliably.

That gives you the perfect support for the argument:

The closed labs still win because they reduce the number of steering interventions.

4. Stronger opening

Original:

GLM 5.2 is a massive jump from GLM 5.1.

Better:

GLM‑5.2 is a massive jump. But the real story is not the benchmark jump — it is the turn tax.

Or:

GLM‑5.2 is the first open-weight model in a while that made me change my routing. But it still has a hidden cost: prompts.

Or best:

GLM‑5.2 is good enough to change the model market. It is not yet good enough to erase the judgment gap.

That opening has tension.

5. Best rewritten version

GLM‑5.2 is a massive jump from GLM‑5.1.But there is a tradeoff people are not talking about: the turn tax.GLM‑5.2 can often accomplish the work. The issue is that you may need three or four prompts to get what GPT‑5.5, Opus 4.8 or Fable 5 would often land in one.That gap does not always show up cleanly on benchmarks. Benchmarks measure whether a model can solve a task. Real work measures how much steering it needs before the output becomes https://t.co/DebLt40L8l it taste. Call it instinct. Call it attention to detail. I think the better name is judgment density: the ability to infer what matters, make the right default choices, preserve context, catch edge cases, and finish the job without being hand-held.Closed labs still have more of that.But the shift is real. We are entering an era where cheaper open-weight models can handle most everyday work. Fable 5 was overkill for 80% of vibe-coding tasks anyway. GLM‑5.2 does not need to be the best model in the world to be the model people use all day.And the timing matters. The Fable 5 shutdown created a sudden gap in the market. https://t.co/8l5VZLWr2F walked straight through it.The lesson should be obvious: when you remove the best closed model from the hands of builders, you do not stop capability diffusion. You accelerate substitution.Restore Fable 5.

The AI race is not only about who ships most often. It is about who compounds the most between releases.

ship → collect user feedback → patch behaviour → ship again → dominate attention → keep enterprise buyers warm.

    • Handoff（跨设备任务迁移）：@dotey 指出，Codex 的新功能可以将未完成的编码任务，连同完整的 Git 状态，无缝迁移到远程服务器继续运行，并在之后拉回本地。他认为这解决了开发者“写码到中途必须离开”的实际痛点。
• Skill 生态的成熟与迭代：@dotey 分享了他的 Skill 迭代方法论（发现问题 -> AI 分析 -> 出方案 -> 确认并更新 Skill），并展示了其 `baoyu-design` Skill 如何进化到能为 PPT 和视频自动添加 AI 配图。@vista8 也宣布正在开发一款集抓取、生图、设计于一体的全能 PPT Skill。

趋势三：设计工具的 AI 能力泛化
AI 正在改变设计的门槛和方法。
• Figma 的网页转设计能力：@vista8 发现 Figma 推出的 Chrome 插件，可以直接将任意网页元素转化为可编辑的设计图层，认为这将“降维打击”网页仿站工作。
• 去 AI 味的 UI 设计方法：@Pluvio9yte 推荐了 `getdesign.md` 项目，该方法通过收集 Linear、Notion 等知名公司的设计规范文件，喂给 Claude Code，从而让 AI 生成的 UI 遵循专业规则，减少“AI 感”。

▫️ 2. 值得注意的独特观点或行业前瞻

• 从“相关性”到“因果性”的范式转移：
    @Pluvio9yte 长篇分析了 Aether AI 提出的“因果大模型”方向。他指出，当前的大模型大多基于数据相关性进行模仿，缺乏对物理世界因果机制的理解（例如无法推理“往有洞的杯子里倒水，水会漏”）。他援引黄碧薇教授的观点，认为引入因果推理，让 AI 理解环境变量、机制和干预结果，是应对具身智能、材料研发等逻辑严谨性要求高的领域的下一个重要变量。
• “Contract First”的开发哲学：
    @Pluvio9yte 结合自己从安全从业者转向全栈开发的经历，提出了一个核心观点：Vibe Coding 的最佳实践并非 Requirement First 或 Code First，而是 Contract First（契约优先）。他认为，在需求不断变化的大项目中，提前定义好 API 契约和数据模型，是让人和 AI 能步调一致、不漂移的关键。
• AI 增效率未必然增福祉的反思：
    @ruanyf 转发了一篇来自黑客新闻的文章，提出了一个尖锐问题：如果 AI 让人们几小时就能完成一周的工作，公司是否应该放假一天？他尖锐地指出，如果不降工时、不涨薪，“那么 AI 对员工的意义是什么？” 对此，@lijigang 也辩证地评论道，Token 消耗量和账单是“虚假指标”，真正需要关注的是“你的问题是否因AI而变好”这一真实指标。
• 端侧模型体量的“天花板”观察：
    @zhixianio 对 Gemma 4 12B Coder 的评测提供了一个冷静的视角。他发现，即使经过微调，12B 规模的模型在处理“长篇、有状态、一次成型”的复杂程序时，能力仍然有明确上限。微调提升的是效率和收敛速度，但抬不高模型的基础能力天花板。

author: y0tafomo
text:
Something just got smarter inside ChatGPT and nobody at OpenAI is saying anything.

This week alone, dozens of testers noticed the exact same thing 🧵

Across X, testers spent two days swapping screenshots and stopwatch times, all pointing to one theory: 

OpenAI is quietly A/B testing GPT-5.6 inside ChatGPT for some users.

The clearest signal is time, not quality.

One tester built a one-prompt 3D browser game with physics and camera controls. It took just over an hour — versus GPT-5.5 Pro's usual 10-minute mark.

Another tester said response times stretched to 20 or 40 minutes, a pace that hadn't shown up since before GPT-5.5 shipped.

Slower isn't always worse. Sometimes it means the model is actually thinking through something harder.

Not everyone is convinced it's a clean win.

One AI benchmarker ran the same spaceship-building prompt on both models. The suspected GPT-5.6 took 87 minutes against GPT-5.5 Extra High's 34 minutes — and Fable 5 still beat both on core geometry.

Leaked specs floating around are specific enough to feel real.

A knowledge cutoff pushed to December 2025. A reasoning-effort setting allegedly raised from 768 to 960. A release candidate nicknamed Kindle-Alpha.

Here's why the timing matters.

China's open-source GLM-5.2 trails Claude Opus 4.8 by just one point on a major engineering benchmark, while beating GPT-5.5 outright on the same test.

And Anthropic just handed every competitor a gap to fill.

Mythos 5 and Fable 5 remain pulled under a US export control directive, leaving the top of the market wide open.

Polymarket traders aren't waiting for confirmation.

Contracts on a GPT-5.6 launch between June 22 and June 28 priced as high as 89% this week.

The market already thinks this is real.

OpenAI still hasn't said a word.

Really strong approach by Harvey. Vertical legal apps are getting pressure from frontier labs, MCP-style plugins, and broader platform plays, but Harvey’s edge is not just access to models. It is the domain depth around them: lawyers, legal workflows, firm-specific feedback loops, benchmarks, private evals, and real client environments.

Especially after what happened with Fable/Mythos, sovereign AI feels less like a buzzword and more like enterprise infrastructure. Law firms, governments, and large enterprises will want more control over their models, data, deployment, and learning loops.

For legal AI, the hard part is not only post-training. It is building the ontology, environment layer, and feedback system that teaches the model how real legal work actually happens. 

Harvey has a real shot because they are combining frontier model strategy with deep domain expertise and client-specific learning.
